# Evaluating ∫ -2x⁴ sin(x) dx

I'll use **tabular integration** (repeated integration by parts), differentiating the polynomial and integrating the trig function.

## Setting Up the Table

| Sign | Differentiate (−2x⁴) | Integrate (sin x) |
|:----:|:---------------------:|:-----------------:|
| +    | −2x⁴                | sin(x)            |
| −    | −8x³                | −cos(x)           |
| +    | −24x²               | −sin(x)           |
| −    | −48x                | cos(x)            |
| +    | −48                 | sin(x)            |
| −    | 0                   | −cos(x)           |

## Multiplying Along Diagonals

$$+(-2x^4)(-\cos x) = 2x^4\cos(x)$$
$$-(-8x^3)(-\sin x) = -8x^3\sin(x)$$
$$+(-24x^2)(\cos x) = -24x^2\cos(x)$$
$$-(-48x)(\sin x) = 48x\sin(x)$$
$$+(-48)(-\cos x) = 48\cos(x)$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
- d/dx[2x⁴cos(x)] = 8x³cos(x) − 2x⁴sin(x)
- d/dx[−8x³sin(x)] = −24x²sin(x) − 8x³cos(x)
- d/dx[−24x²cos(x)] = −48xcos(x) + 24x²sin(x)
- d/dx[48xsin(x)] = 48sin(x) + 48xcos(x)
- d/dx[48cos(x)] = −48sin(x)

All terms cancel except **−2x⁴sin(x)** ✓

## Final Answer

$$2x^4\cos(x) - 8x^3\sin(x) - 24x^2\cos(x) + 48x\sin(x) + 48\cos(x) + C$$

<answer>2*x**4*cos(x) - 8*x**3*sin(x) - 24*x**2*cos(x) + 48*x*sin(x) + 48*cos(x) + C</answer>

8x³ cos(x) - 2x⁴ sin(x) - 24x² sin(x) - 8x³ cos(x) - 48x cos(x) + 24x² sin(x) + 48 sin(x) + 48x cos(x) - 48 sin(x)

= -2x⁴ sin(x) ✓

So the answer is: 2*x**4*cos(x) - 8*x**3*sin(x) - 24*x**2*cos(x) + 48*x*sin(x) + 48*cos(x) + C
